summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and ensure you are using version 22w13a.
2. Create a new Creative mode world with default settings.
3. Teleport to a far away structure such as a woodland mansion or pillager outpost that may contain naturally generated allays.
4. Observe if the chunks near you are loading in.
5. If they aren't loading, reload chunks using F3 + A and observe again.
6. If chunks still do not load after reloading, teleport closer to the structure.
7. If chunks still do not load even when closer to the structure, you have successfully reproduced this bug.
8. Observe that the game hangs, commands do not work, and UI elements such as gamemode switcher do nothing.
9. Note that attempting to save the world or use F3 + C does not work; you must force crash the game using system-specific methods (e.g., Task Manager on Windows, terminal command on Linux).
Observed Behavior:
When a player teleports to a distant location containing structures with naturally generated allays, such as woodland mansions or pillager outposts, the game server hangs and stops responding. The chunks surrounding these structures fail to load properly, causing the entire area to become unresponsive. Despite this issue, the F3 debug menu remains functional and displays an internal server tick rate of 18ms, but it does not facilitate further chunk loading. Attempting to reload chunks using the F3 A command is ineffective. The game becomes completely unresponsive, preventing any commands or UI interactions from functioning correctly.

If a player attempts to save the world while the chunks are failing to load, they will be unable to do so and must force crash the game, resulting in no data being saved. Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not trigger this issue, nor does visiting a woodland mansion without naturally generated allays. The bug is specific only to structures with naturally generated allays.

To reproduce this issue, teleport to a structure that may contain naturally generated allays and observe if the chunks near you are loading in. If they do not load, attempt to reload them using F3 A. If the chunks still fail to load, it indicates successful reproduction of the bug. This bug affects Minecraft version 22w13a but is likely patched in future snapshots.

Exiting the game while this issue occurs requires manually ending the process through task manager on Windows, killing the OpenJDK process via terminal on Linux, or using force quit options on MacOS.
Expected Behavior: When teleporting near a structure containing naturally generated allays, chunks should load normally without any lag or freezing. The F3 menu and UI elements should function correctly, allowing for smooth interaction. Commands and gamemode switches should work as expected, and saving the world should not be hindered. No chunk-loading issues should occur, even when close to structures with allays.
